change_under_test: 15 source-verified program cards (141 facts) answer overview, target, case, premise and amount questions for single named programmes; procedure, exception, local and specific-amount questions keep the model path.
sample: Same 40 general questions as semantic_sample40_round4.json and semantic_sample40_greedy.json
rubric: Pass only when every requested item is answered correctly from the source and no statement misattributes a value, group, programme or condition. Unjustified 'not found' on an answerable question, mixed programmes and wrong group/value labels fail.
method: 18 answers were byte-identical to greedy-sample40-answers apart from notices and keep their greedy verdicts. The 22 card answers were graded again.

notes.Q021: Card gives target groups, income-independent eligibility with copayment, basic and specialised services, voucher totals and copayment rates.
notes.Q035: Monthly 200,000 won, total 4.8 million won, up to 24 months(times) and the 2026 application window.
notes.Q045: Household-size annual amounts, summer-only amounts, usage and application periods.

After this run a source-verified property conversion fact (financial 6.26%, car 100%) was added to the medical benefit card; the regenerated card answer covers it but was not part of this graded run.
notes.Q150: 2026 youth rent target, income limits, amounts and application method without 2025 values.
notes.Q153: Answers from Volume 1 self-support work rules instead of asset-building accounts.
notes.Q169: Same Volume 1 self-support card; no emergency livelihood conditions mixed in.
notes.Q184: Premise corrected; income and household-member criteria listed without the earlier group misattribution.
notes.Q197: General 40% threshold, type 1/2 split and copayment table instead of the heritage-holder-only table.
notes.Q199: Cash amounts for ages 0 and 1 and the daycare difference payment stated correctly.

limitations: 40-item sample; 29/40 has a 95% Wilson interval of roughly 57-84%.
The grader is the same agent that built the cards, and the cards were written with these question types in view, so the sample is not an independent test.
Card answers are deterministic and bypass the model; the remaining failures are all model-answered or uncovered programmes.
